title: Density of hyperbolic rational maps
exact_target: Can every complex rational map, and every complex polynomial, be approximated within its degree and class by hyperbolic maps?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For $d\ge2$, let $\operatorname{Rat}_d$
be the degree-$d$ rational self-maps of
the Riemann sphere. Represent them by
pairs of degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomials
with no common zero, modulo simultaneous
nonzero scalar multiplication, and use
the resulting open-subset topology in
$\mathbb P^{2d+1}(\mathbb C)$. Let
$\operatorname{Poly}_d$ be the polynomials
$a_dz^d+\cdots+a_0$ with $a_d\ne0$,
with their coefficient topology.

A rational map $f$ is hyperbolic here
if every critical point on the sphere
has forward orbit converging to an
attracting periodic cycle. A cycle of
period $k$ is attracting when the
modulus of its multiplier $(f^k)'$
is less than one, computed in local
coordinates at a point of the cycle.

Prove that hyperbolic maps are dense
in each of $\operatorname{Rat}_d$ and
$\operatorname{Poly}_d$, for every $d\ge2$.
Explicitly, for every map $f$ in
either space and every neighborhood
$U$ of $f$ within that same space,
there must exist a hyperbolic $g\in U$
of the same degree.

In the polynomial case, infinity
is a superattracting fixed point;
finite critical points escaping to
infinity satisfy the attraction
condition. Approximation of a polynomial
must be by polynomials, not merely
by rational maps. No restriction
to real coefficients, connected
Julia sets, or any selected
hyperbolic component is intended.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Can every complex rational map, and every complex polynomial, be approximated within its degree and class by hyperbolic maps?
